question:
The pineapple was first domesticated in South America, and its physical form no longer matches that of the wild plant from which it descends. Summer squash likewise _______ its wild ancestor. That ancestral plant had a tough rind and bitter flesh, but Indigenous peoples in eastern North America bred the crop over time until its rind grew soft and its flesh mild-tasting.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The pineapple's form no longer matches its wild ancestor, and "likewise" signals that summer squash also differs from its ancestor, so "varies from" (differs from) fits.
longexplanation: The passage sets up a comparison: the pineapple no longer looks identical to its wild ancestor, and the word "likewise" tells us summer squash does the same thing. The following sentences describe how squash was bred from a tough rind and bitter flesh to a soft rind and mild flesh, which is clear evidence of a difference between the crop and its ancestor. The blank therefore must express difference, and "varies from" means differs from. The remaining choices—"helpful with," "argues with," and "reacts to"—do not convey difference and do not fit the logic of the sentence.

question:
The mark of William Shakespeare's writing can be seen plainly across a huge range of later literary works, and it is just as _______ in many creations in other media, from fine art (such as Edward Alcock's painting Portia and Shylock) to popular music (such as the musician Elvis Costello's song "Miss Macbeth").

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: "Seen plainly" in the first clause is echoed by "just as," so the parallel word must mean obvious or visible; "apparent" fits.
longexplanation: The sentence states that Shakespeare's influence "can be seen plainly" in literary works and is "just as ___" in other media. The phrase "just as" signals that the blank should match the earlier idea of being plainly visible. "Apparent" means readily seen or obvious, which is parallel to "seen plainly." "Subtle" is nearly the opposite, while "unusual" and "excessive" have nothing to do with visibility, so only "apparent" completes the comparison logically.

question:
Maryam Hosseini and her colleagues trained a computer program to recognize sidewalks using aerial photographs of thoroughly mapped areas of Manhattan. When the program was later tested on images of Brooklyn, it _______ identified sidewalks in the great majority of cases and could even tell whether a sidewalk was concrete or cobblestone. Hosseini expects that this already-strong performance will improve as the program is used more widely.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The program's "already-strong performance" means it identified sidewalks accurately, so "reliably" fits the blank.
longexplanation: The passage reports that the program identified sidewalks in the great majority of cases and could even distinguish concrete from cobblestone, then labels this an "already-strong performance." The blank must describe successful, dependable identification, which "reliably" captures. "Clumsily," "rarely," and "slowly" all contradict the description of strong, accurate performance, so "reliably" is the only precise choice.

question:
This passage is adapted from Anthony Trollope's 1855 novel The Warden. Charles James is the son of a senior member of the clergy.

Charles James was an exact and careful boy; he never committed himself; he well knew how much was expected from the eldest son of the Archdeacon of Barchester, and was therefore mindful not to mix too freely with other boys. He had not the great talents of his younger brothers, but he exceeded them in judgment and propriety of demeanour; his fault, if he had one, was an over-attention to words instead of things; there was a thought too much finesse about him, and, as even his father sometimes told him, he was too fond of a compromise.

Which choice best states the function of the phrase “if he had one” in the text as a whole?
option a: It acknowledges that the qualities in Charles James the narrator goes on to describe may not actually be undesirable characteristics.
option b: It concedes that Charles James's attempts to be held in respect are sometimes fruitless.
option c: It signals a shift in focus from describing Charles James's good qualities to criticizing his tendency to place too much value on artfulness.
option d: It anticipates readers' objections to the narrator's criticism of Charles James's faults.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The hedge "if he had one" casts doubt on whether Charles James truly has a fault, suggesting the traits described may not really be flaws.
longexplanation: Just before the phrase, the narrator writes "his fault, if he had one." The qualifier "if he had one" introduces doubt about whether the characteristics that follow—over-attention to words, excess finesse, fondness for compromise—are genuinely faults at all. This softens the criticism and admits the traits might not be undesirable, which matches choice A. Choices B, C, and D misread the hedging function of the phrase, treating it as a concession about respect, a shift into criticism, or an anticipation of reader objections rather than a qualification of whether a fault exists.

question:
The Nazca lines of Peru are enormous designs that ancient peoples etched into the ground. Monuments such as these helped inspire the land art movement, which emerged in the 1960s. Artists in this movement produce pieces situated in outdoor settings. Dennis Oppenheim's 1968 work Annual Rings, for instance, consists of concentric lines resembling tree rings that he cut into the ice covering a waterway.

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
option a: The text describes the benefits of being an artist.
option b: The text argues against placing works of art outside.
option c: The text describes the popularity of art galleries in the 1960s.
option d: The text provides information about the land art movement.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The text defines the land art movement and offers Oppenheim's Annual Rings as an example, so its purpose is to inform readers about that movement.
longexplanation: The passage introduces the Nazca lines as an inspiration, states that the land art movement began in the 1960s, explains that its artists create outdoor works, and gives Oppenheim's 1968 Annual Rings as an illustration. Everything in the text serves to inform the reader about the land art movement, which is choice D. The text does not argue against outdoor art (B), discuss the popularity of galleries (C), or describe the benefits of being an artist (A).

question:
Steve Carter's award-winning play Eden was staged in 1976 by the pioneering Negro Ensemble Company (NEC). One of NEC's cofounders, Douglas Turner Ward—an actor, director, and playwright—had met the actor and producer Robert Hooks in 1960 while the two were touring in a production of Lorraine Hansberry's play A Raisin in the Sun. The pair imagined a theater company devoted to developing and spotlighting the work of Black theater professionals. Since NEC was founded in 1967, its workshops and performances have given Black playwrights, Carter among them, a platform for their compelling stories.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
option a: It illustrates the widespread influence of a play discussed earlier in the text.
option b: It provides additional information about a person mentioned in the text.
option c: It emphasizes the ongoing significance of the theater company discussed in the text.
option d: It explains the circumstances that led to the formation of the theater company discussed in the text.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The final sentence stresses that since 1967 NEC has continued to give Black playwrights a platform, underscoring the company's lasting importance.
longexplanation: The underlined sentence notes that since NEC's founding in 1967, its workshops and performances have provided Black playwrights, including Carter, a platform for their stories. By pointing to what NEC has done "since" its founding, the sentence highlights the theater company's continuing significance, which matches choice C. It does not add detail about a single person (B) or explain how the company was formed (D)—ideas the earlier sentences handle—nor does it illustrate a play's influence (A).

question:
Total Areas of Five Pueblo Nations in New Mexico

| Tribal nation | Area (square miles) |
| --- | --- |
| Pueblo of Acoma | 595.7 |
| Taos Pueblo | 156.2 |
| Pueblo of Sandia | 38.9 |
| Pueblo de Cochiti | 82.1 |
| Pueblo of Pojoaque | 21.4 |

Of the nineteen Pueblo tribal nations in New Mexico, the Pueblo of Laguna is the largest, spanning close to 800 square miles. Most Pueblo tribal nations, however, are far smaller. The Pueblo of Sandia, for example, covers a total area of 38.9 square miles, while the total area of Pueblo de Cochiti is _______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The table lists Pueblo de Cochiti at 82.1 square miles, so that value completes the statement.
longexplanation: The sentence calls for the total area of Pueblo de Cochiti as given in the table. The table lists Pueblo de Cochiti as 82.1 square miles, so choice C supplies exactly the right figure. The other options give the areas of different nations—Taos Pueblo (156.2), Pueblo of Acoma (595.7), and Pueblo of Pojoaque (21.4)—so only choice C accurately completes the statement.

question:
Ratified in 2017 by two-thirds of the World Trade Organization's member nations, the Trade Facilitation Agreement (TFA) is a trade-reform measure meant to cut down on redundant customs procedures and other expensive features of international trade. In a 2021 report, the economist Jayson Beckman modeled the global market prices of several agricultural commodities under two scenarios: the TFA and an alternative reform in which agricultural tariffs (import taxes that generally raise the prices of imported goods) are removed. After reviewing the report's data, a student concludes that, overall, consumers of the commodities listed in the table would likely benefit more from the TFA than from tariff removal.

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the student's claim?
option a: Under the tariff-removal scenario, the average prices of processed foods, wheat, and fruits and vegetables would decrease by more than 1%, while the average price of rice would decrease by less than 1%.
option b: Under the tariff-removal scenario, the average price of processed foods would increase, but the average prices of wheat and rice would decrease.
option c: Under the TFA scenario, the average prices of all four commodities would decrease, whereas under the tariff-removal scenario, only the average price of processed foods would decrease.
option d: Under the TFA scenario, the average price of rice would decrease by a smaller amount than any of the other three commodities' prices would, whereas its average price would increase under the tariff-removal scenario.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Only choice C shows the TFA lowering all four prices while tariff removal lowers just one, supporting that consumers benefit more under the TFA.
longexplanation: The student claims that consumers would benefit more from the TFA than from tariff removal, so the supporting evidence must show broader price decreases under the TFA. Choice C states that under the TFA all four commodities' average prices would fall, whereas under tariff removal only processed foods' price would drop. Lower prices across every commodity benefit consumers, directly backing the claim. The other choices either fail to compare the two scenarios in the student's favor or focus on a single commodity, so they do not support the conclusion.

question:
Great Expectations, an 1861 novel by Charles Dickens, features a narrator who portrays his uncle, Joe Gargery, as at once powerful and tender: ______

Which quotation from Great Expectations most effectively illustrates the claim?
option a: "In his working-clothes, Joe was a well-knit characteristic-looking blacksmith; in his holiday clothes, he was more like a scarecrow in good circumstances, than anything else."
option b: "When I looked back at Joe in the long passage, he was still weighing his hat with the greatest care, and was coming after us in long strides on the tips of his toes."
option c: "There I stood, for minutes, looking at Joe, already at work with a glow of health and strength upon his face that made it show as if the bright sun of the life in store for him were shining on it."
option d: "I have often thought [Joe] since, like the steam-hammer that can crush a man or pat an egg-shell, in his combination of strength with gentleness."
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The steam-hammer image—able to "crush a man or pat an egg-shell"—captures Joe's blend of strength and gentleness.
longexplanation: The claim is that Joe is both powerful and tender. Choice D compares Joe to a steam-hammer that can "crush a man or pat an egg-shell" and explicitly names "his combination of strength with gentleness." This single image conveys power and tenderness at the same time, illustrating the claim precisely. The other quotations describe Joe's clothing, movements, or appearance but never pair strength with gentleness, so only choice D fits.

question:
The towns of Entebbe and Jamame both lie almost directly on the ______ they are in different countries. Entebbe is located in Uganda, while Jamame is in Somalia.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Two independent clauses—"...lie almost directly on the equator" and "they are in different countries"—must be joined with a comma plus the coordinating conjunction "but."
longexplanation: The blank joins two complete sentences: "The towns... lie almost directly on the equator" and "they are in different countries." Linking two independent clauses requires a comma followed by a coordinating conjunction, and "but" also fits the contrast between sharing the equator yet lying in different countries. Choice B, "equator, but," provides exactly that. Choice A produces a run-on, choice C creates a comma splice, and choice D turns the second clause into an ungrammatical relative clause, so only B is correct.

question:
Although they are located in different countries, the towns of Entebbe, Uganda, and Booue, Gabon, ______ They are among the few places that sit almost directly on the equator.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
option b: do they have something in common.
option c: do they have something in common?
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The sentence is a declarative statement, not a question, so it keeps subject-verb order and ends with a period: "do have something in common."
longexplanation: The sentence "the towns of Entebbe, Uganda, and Booue, Gabon, ___" is a statement, and the sentence that follows explains what the towns share. A declarative sentence keeps normal subject-verb order ("do have") and ends with a period, not a question mark. Choice D, "do have something in common.," satisfies both requirements. Choices A and C wrongly add a question mark to a non-question, and choices B and C invert the word order to "do they," which suits a question rather than this statement, so only D is correct.
